domain: alpha : Type*, [DecidableEq alpha], f : Finset alpha -> Int, S : Finset alpha; finiteness of S is intrinsic and the results apply in particular to every finite alpha
definition: coefficient f S = sum T in S.powerset ((-1:Int)^(S.card-T.card) * f T)
shared_bound_hypothesis: h_f : forall T:Finset alpha, T subset S -> abs(f T)<=1

obligations.coefficient_def: forall f S, coefficient f S = sum T in S.powerset ((-1:Int)^(S.card-T.card) * f T)
obligations.zeta_reconstruction: forall f S, sum T in S.powerset (coefficient f T) = f S
obligations.coefficient_abs_bound: forall f S (h_f:forall T, T subset S -> abs(f T)<=1), abs(coefficient f S) <= (2:Int)^S.card
obligations.coefficient_natAbs_bound: forall f S n (h_f:forall T, T subset S -> abs(f T)<=1) (hcard:S.card<=n), Int.natAbs(coefficient f S) < (2:Nat)^(n+1)

supporting_obligations: coefficient_insert: splitting a powerset at a fresh element gives the difference of shifted and unshifted coefficients
Finite-set induction generalizes over f, so it can be applied to the shifted function
Triangle inequality bounds each signed integer term by one and powerset cardinality is 2^S.card
